summary: Three well-written passages (814 / 817 / 880 words) on the history of paper money, car-free days and stage fright, at IELTS length with a good mix of question types. All answer keys hold up, and True/False/Not Given and completion answers follow passage order. The texts are clear and well signposted, so the paper is a little gentler than real IELTS, which is right for B2 students.
strengths: IELTS Academic register; passage 3 has C1 vocabulary and argument (illusion of transparency, miscalibration, arousal curve).
Full IELTS question mix: sentence completion, TFNG, matching information, summary completion, matching people with one extra name, MCQ, YNNG and sentence endings with two spare endings.
MCQ distractors reverse or distort details of the passage (e.g. precise skills 'the last to be affected'), as in the real test.
NOT GIVEN items (Marco Polo bringing notes home, polymer note costs, stage fright becoming more common) are genuinely unaddressed.

issues.problem: Paraphrase pair used 'levels of noise', which is not in the summary as written ('levels of {{22}}').
issues.change: Pair is now ['hearing birdsong in the city centre', 'birdsong to be heard in the centre'].

issues.problem: Some existing pairs matched opposite meanings ('refused to believe' / 'accepted') rather than the same meaning.
issues.change: Replaced with same-meaning pairs (Q8 ['described it at length in the account', 'Marco Polo's description'], Q10 ['had been abandoned', 'stopped using']).

issues.problem: Q16 (paragraph E) and Q24 (Vela) test the same sentence, so a student who gets one gets both.
issues.change: Suggest replacing Q16 with the displacement point in paragraph E: 'a problem caused by traffic moving to other roads'.

issues.problem: Ending A 'judged speakers to be calmer than the speakers expected' is copied almost word for word from the passage.
issues.change: Suggest 'thought the speakers looked more relaxed than the speakers believed they did'.

issues.problem: Passage 1 sentence completions keep the passage wording around the gap ('made of iron', 'bark of mulberry trees', 'signature of the bank's cashier'), so they are easier than real IELTS items.
issues.change: For extra challenge, paraphrase the prompts, e.g. Q5 'Every early Bank of England note was signed by its ______'.
